correct_answer: Revised methodology — the loan sat in an early-adoption portfolio at the time the attestation was filed (March 15), so early adoption follows the loan regardless of subsequent transfer
rationale: The critical signal is in the Teams thread where Robert Nakamura initially states that phase-in election follows 'where they sit today' (the receiving portfolio). However, this general guidance is contradicted by the specific timeline facts: the attestation was filed March 15, 2025, and the loan's operational transfer did not occur until March 28 (and settlement not until March 31). At the time the early-adoption attestation was filed, this loan was still booked in the Piedmont (wealth management) portfolio. The attestation bound all positions in that portfolio as of the attestation date. The OCC FAQ (referenced in SharePoint version history) and standard regulatory practice holds that early adoption elections are irrevocable and attach to positions held at election time. Answer A is wrong because grandfathering applies to origination date relative to the final rule's compliance deadline, not to calculation methodology during phase-in. Answer B incorrectly applies Robert's casual Teams guidance without accounting for the fact that the transfer occurred AFTER the attestation locked in the election for existing positions. Answer D gets the right answer but for the wrong reason — Section 4.1's June 1 date applies to 'new credit extensions,' not existing positions that transferred between books.
